messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging SRE oncall — multi-region failover oscillation detected for production routing; automated failover triggered between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 repeatedly. Initial alert 1769994321.

alice: i'm on it — seeing spike in 5xx from public API (~7% error rate), frontend traces show upstream timeouts around 1769994322.

mike: checking infra dashboards — backend health probes are flapping in us-east. but routing table shows failover toggles every ~20s. looks like a re-converge loop.

raj: digging into DNS side — noticed inconsistent A answers from our global resolver cluster; different POPs returning different region IPs. TTLs are 60s but control-plane pushed a restore earlier and some edges still had old records. possible split-horizon / propagation lag.

kim: run dig from multiple places:
```
# from my laptop (8.8.8.8)
dig +short api.redwood.local @8.8.8.8
34.82.12.9
# from eu probe
dig +short api.redwood.local @1.1.1.1
18.205.1.3
```
these switch back/forth.

alice: logs show LB->backend 504s then healthy again, then 502s after DNS flips. healthcheck latencies spike during the flip window. suspect control plane autoscaler/eviction events in eu-west causing transient backend unreachability, then our failover policy moves traffic, which hits us-east, then eu-west comes back and traffic shifts again.

mike: i can pause automated regional failover in the control plane, set failover to manual to stop the oscillation. doing it now.

raj: noted. i'm preparing a sticky-routing rule to pin current active VIPs to us-east for 10m while we stabilize. applying: 
```
apiGateway.failoverPolicy = "manual"
apiGateway.preferredRegion = "us-east-1"
apiGateway.failoverCooldown = 600  # seconds
```

support-lead: customer impact — alerting support and PG. Top affected customers: AcmeCorp (high traffic), NovaPay. Error rates + latency visible in SLAs. preparing customer status page update: "degraded: some customers seeing intermittent 5xx when requests cross regions."

alice: i pushed a quick probe to compare health across pods: lots of evictions in eu-west nodepool 3, kernel OOM messages around same time as failovers. root-cause might be noisy deploy + insufficient pod disruption budget.

kim: can we revert the recent autoscaling/deploy in eu-west? it's a risky rollback but might stop the churn.

mike: holding on full rollback until we have sticky routing in place. otherwise traffic could keep bouncing. sticky routing is active — i've disabled automatic failover in the control plane and set prefer_region=us-east-1.

raj: routing change applied at 1769994460. confirming dig now returns us-east IP from all probes.

kim: curl smoke:
```
curl -sS -D - https://api.redwood.local/health | head -n 5
HTTP/2 200
...
```
healthchecks green from us-east testers.

support-lead: posting interim status to customers now. will escalate to exec if SLA breach threshold looks likely.

alice: handing on-call to mike for mitigation & monitoring — i've captured initial logs and will do postmortem doc. mike, i leave you the live console. tagging for 1h handoff.

mike: taking over, ack. I'll monitor error rate and keep sticky routing for 30m then reevaluate. opening incident ticket INC-2026-487.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to P1 by alice at 1769994480. On-call: mike. Handoff recorded.

raj: mitigation checklist executed: 
- disabled automated failover
- applied prefer_region pin
- disabled recent autoscaler rule in eu-west
- raised pod disruption budgets for critical deployments
- scaled up eu-west nodepool slowly to drain less aggressively

kim: after mitigations, error rate dropped to ~0.6% and latency normalized. keeping eyes for 20m for any re-oscillation.

support-lead: customer comms sent: short message + ETA 1h for next update. logged affected customers and severity.

alice: assigning postmortem owner to raj. include timeline, DNS TTL/propagation issues, autoscaler/deploy interplay, and recommend: staggered deploys, increase default DNS TTL during planned failovers, and improve healthcheck thresholds.

mike: i'll keep the incident channel open and send final "resolved" when we revert manual pins and validate stability. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Resolved flag will be set once manual failover pins are removed and 30m stability confirmed. Next update expected by 1769994920."
